transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sam Park (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Ava Brooks (Redwood CSM); Raj Patel (CTO), Maya Chen (Cloud Eng), Oliver Stone (Head of Sec), Hannah Li (PM)

Optional summary (auto):
- POC scoping for private networking and data residency. Primary ask: run a 4-week POC in a private VPC deployment with VPC peering or PrivateLink to avoid public egress.
- Success criteria: p95 latency < 200ms for typical 128-token generation, cost target <$0.015/token equivalent, no sensitive data leaving region, SOC2-compliant audit trails.
- Workload sizing: plan for bursts to 500 RPS (inference requests), sustained 100 RPS, mixed short/long sequences (64-1024 tokens).
- Next steps and actions listed below.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sam Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sam from Redwood, AE on the account. Lina and Ava are with me, SE and CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Raj Patel: Good, thanks. Busy but excited.
[00:09] Maya Chen: Hey, Maya here. Quick heads up, apologies if connection gets a lil spotty, we're on wired but, you know.
[00:13] Sam Park: No worries. Goal for today is to scope the POC for private networking and data residency, nail down success criteria, workload sizing, and timelines. We want to make sure the POC exercise mirrors your production constraints.
[00:25] Hannah Li: Yep, we want realistic traffic and the security bar high — egress restrictions are a must.
[00:29] Lina Gomez: Great. Can we start with your current infra shape and what you consider sensitive? Maya or Raj?
[00:35] Raj Patel: Sure. We're running most services in us-east-1, some DR in eu-west-1. Sensitive PHI lives in our EMR system, but for the POC we'll use de-identified records. However, network egress to public endpoints is blocked by policy unless it's via approved PrivateLink endpoints or peered VPCs. So direct public internet calls from our VPC are a no-go.
[00:55] Oliver Stone: Also, audit logs need to be retained for at least 2 years and integrated with our SIEM. KMS keys must be customer-managed in our AWS account.
[01:05] Sam Park: Understood. Redwood Private supports VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for routed traffic, and we can integrate with customer KMS for disk encryption. Quick note: there are tradeoffs between peering and PrivateLink — peering is lower latency and simpler for cross-AZ traffic, PrivateLink is more restrictive but often easier for strict egress policies. Lina, can you walk through the network flows?
[01:25] Lina Gomez: Yeah. So option A: VPC peering to a Redwood-managed VPC in the same region — we'd provision endpoints in us-east-1 and you peer. Traffic stays on AWS backbone. Option B: AWS PrivateLink — we publish an NLB-backed endpoint service in our account and you create an endpoint in yours. PrivateLink gives you tighter control over which subnets can talk to the service, but it uses NLB -> slightly higher lat. In our experience maybe 5-20ms extra p95 depending on region. Also we can support Transit Gateway if you use that.
[02:00] Maya Chen: Do you support cross-region peering? We may want to put POC in us-east-1 but production might go to eu-west-1 for data residency.
[02:08] Lina Gomez: Yes. We can deploy private control plane replicas in multiple regions. For the POC we'd recommend keeping it in your primary region (us-east-1) to remove cross-region variability for the first benchmark. For production we can replicate and route by policy.
[02:22] Raj Patel: Sounds good. On workload: our product does short retrieval + generation flows. Typical payloads are ~128 tokens output, sometimes larger up to 512-1024 for long responses. We expect sustained 100 RPS during business hours and spikes to 500 RPS for batch ops.
[02:40] Lina Gomez: Perfect. For benchmarking we'll simulate both mixed short (128) and long (512–1024) sequences. For sizing we need to know average input tokens, expected concurrency, and whether KV cache priming will be used. Do you plan to use prefix caching?
[02:55] Hannah Li: We do use repeated system prompts and many similar requests; caching would help. But for the POC we want to measure both cold and warm cache performance.
[03:03] Sam Park: Great — success criteria? What does PivotalCare need to call the POC successful?
[03:09] Raj Patel: Primary: latency SLO — p95 under 200ms for 128-token outputs on warm cache. Secondary: throughput meeting sustained 100 RPS with sub-1s median for 512 token responses. Security: zero public egress, KMS customer keys, audit logs into our SIEM. Cost: show projection that per-inference cost is below our internal threshold — targeting less than $0.015 per 128-token equivalent.
[03:36] Oliver Stone: And we need proof of encryption at rest and in transit, plus SOC2 info and penetration test reports.
[03:44] Sam Park: Totally — we'll drop the security packet and SOC2 + penetration summary. We support BYOK via AWS KMS, and we can route audit logs to your CloudWatch or S3 bucket with the retention you want. Lina, on bench harness?
[03:56] Lina Gomez: We'll provide a benchmark harness that runs scenarios: 100 RPS sustained, 500 RPS burst, mixed token lengths. We'll run cold/warm cache runs and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and token throughput. We'll also capture egress bandwidth to confirm no public paths used. We'll share a spreadsheet with results and runbook.
[04:18] Maya Chen: For the PrivateLink peering choice — what's the setup time and what permissions do we need?
[04:23] Lina Gomez: PrivateLink: you'll need to create an Interface Endpoint in your VPC, accepting the service from our account; permissions revolve around VPC endpoint creation and security groups. Setup can be done in a few hours once we share the endpoint service. VPC peering requires route table edits; it's quick too but if you have strict route control it can take longer to approve. We'll provide IaC snippets for both.
[04:43] Raj Patel: Any egress charges we should be aware of? We want to avoid unexpected cross-account data egress costs.
[04:49] Sam Park: If traffic stays in-region via peering or PrivateLink, there aren't public internet egress charges, but cross-AZ/data transfer between accounts can still incur AWS data transfer fees depending on path. We'll include an estimate. For cross-region replication there will be inter-region data transfer fees.
[05:04] Oliver Stone: For compliance, we need an allowlist of IPs and the ability to rotate certs and KMS keys.
[05:10] Lina Gomez: We can provide static outbound IPs for egress if you need them. For the KMS rotation, if you manage the CMK in your account we don't have access to the key material; rotation is on your cadence.
[05:22] Hannah Li: Timeline — what's realistic for a 4-week POC?
[05:25] Sam Park: Typical POC timeline: Week 0: Kickoff + networking setup (VPC peering or PrivateLink). Week 1: baseline benchmark (cold), Week 2: tuning (batching, quantization suggestions), Week 3: warm-cache benchmark + security reviews, Week 4: report + recommendations and decision. So about 3–4 weeks.
[05:44] Raj Patel: Can we accelerate to 3 weeks if networking goes quickly?
[05:47] Lina Gomez: Possibly; if we get traces and sample data ahead of time we can pre-provision and run early.
[05:53] Maya Chen: We'll send traces and current RPS profile today. Also need the runbook and sample Terraform.
[05:58] Sam Park: We'll send Private Networking runbook, CF/Terraform snippets for both peering and PrivateLink, and the security packet. Lina will send benchmark harness.
[06:06] Oliver Stone: Last question — model variants and quantization: do you support quantized LLMs that still meet quality bar?
[06:12] Lina Gomez: Yes, Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and we can test quality regressions against your eval prompts. For POC we'll test a baseline fp16 variant and a lower-bit quantized variant to show tradeoffs.
[06:23] Raj Patel: Good. Also include a simple AB test plan for rollout in production if POC passes.
[06:28] Sam Park: Noted.
[06:30] Ava Brooks: I'll schedule the follow-up and ensure the security packet goes to Oliver.
[06:33] Hannah Li: Thanks everyone.
[06:35] Sam Park: Recap of next steps: Redwood to share runbook, security docs, and benchmark harness; PivotalCare to share traces and approve networking approach. We'll target the baseline benchmark week of 2026-04-27 and follow-up 2026-04-29 to lock config.
[06:50] Raj Patel: Thanks all.
[06:53] Meeting ends.
